channel.title: Global Competition Review - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Global Competition Review (globalcompetitionreview.com)

item.title: DOJ’s Glad downplays “trial risk” with whistleblowers
item.description: The Department of Justice’s top official for criminal antitrust matters has rejected criticism that juries will not trust trial testimony from witnesses that stand to gain financial awards for their cooperation.

item.title: Vacancies: The Briefing for 4 March 2026
item.description: Booking has found an accommodating bedfellow in the Amsterdam District Court after the latter threatened to throw out an antitrust lawsuit against the platform unless claimant hotels fully evidence alleged damages caused by its narrow price parity clauses. Also in The Briefing, the European Commission begins advertising internally for a candidate to permanently fill the vacant director general for...

item.title: UK tribunal sets trial date for Motorola collective action
item.description: A six-week trial for a £650 million mass lawsuit accusing Motorola of overcharging the UK government and emergency services for its mobile radio network services is set to begin at the start of October 2027.

item.title: A Q&A with Matthew Boswell
item.description: Canada’s Competition Bureau is already making use of new structural presumptions baked into the country’s merger control rules, according to the agency’s former head. In an interview with GCR, newly appointed Norton Rose Fulbright partner Matthew Boswell discussed recent antitrust reforms, potential divergence with the US during deal reviews, and the prospect of ministers ordering the agency to co...

item.title: CAT challenges class representative’s remuneration package in salmon claim
item.description: The UK’s Competition Appeal Tribunal has criticised Anne Heal’s hourly charge-out rate as the proposed class representative in a collective action against several major farmed salmon producers.

item.title: Competition policy issues a major concern for constituents, UK lawmaker says
item.description: UK voters are becoming increasingly mindful of competition policy issues amid mounting cost-of-living pressures and increased consolidation within markets, according to the chair of an influential parliamentary committee.

item.title: UK cinemas “cannot rely” on EU to remedy potential effects of Paramount/WB, association says
item.description: Potential competition risks resulting from Paramount’s acquisition of Warner Bros would be “additionally” felt in the UK compared to other European markets, according to the head of the UK Cinema Association.

item.title: Ticketmaster used Live Nation ties for “threats”, arena execs say
item.description: A Ticketmaster executive made “credible threats” that Live Nation would withhold concerts from a venue in Minnesota if it used a rival’s ticketing platform, a witness called by the Department of Justice has alleged.

item.title: High hurdles: The Tipline for 4 March 2026
item.description: NewsGuard may have a harder time getting a Federal Trade Commission probe blocked than Media Matters did. Judge Dabney Friedrich frequently pressed the news rating organisation during a hearing on Wednesday to justify its need for a preliminary injunction. item.title: Google agrees to share app catalogue in new Epic settlement
item.description: Google and Epic Games have restructured their settlement proposal in an attempt to appease concerns that their prior agreement upended key aspects of the permanent injunction issued by the US District Court for the Northern District of California.
